questions.q: **CGKN : EIMP :: DJOT : ?**
questions.solution: Each letter of CGKN moves 2 places forward to give EIMP (C to E, G to I, K to M, N to P). Applying +2 to DJOT gives **FLQV**.
questions.shortcut: +2 throughout: D to F, J to L, O to Q, T to V.

questions.solution: 3 × 5 = 15 and 4 × 6 = 24 — the second number is **n × (n + 2)**. So 6 × 8 = **48**.

questions.q: **Chef : Knife :: Tailor : ?**
questions.solution: A chef's working tool is the knife; a tailor's working tool is the **needle**. Shirt is the product, cloth is the raw material, and a machine is not the hand tool that parallels the knife.
questions.shortcut: Second word = the trade's tool, not its product or material.

questions.q: Find the odd group of letters: **ADG, BEH, SVY, OQT**
questions.solution: In ADG, BEH and SVY the gap between consecutive letters is +3, +3 (A to D to G etc.). In OQT the gaps are +2 then +3 (O to Q to T), so **OQT** is the odd one.
questions.shortcut: Write the letter gaps under each cluster.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: **125, 216, 343, 400**
questions.solution: 125 = 5³, 216 = 6³ and 343 = 7³ are perfect cubes; 400 is not a cube (it is 20²). Odd one: **400**.
questions.shortcut: Check cubes first: 5³, 6³, 7³ … 400 is not among them.

questions.q: Find the missing term: **5, 11, 23, 47, ?**
questions.shortcut: ×2 + 1 throughout.

questions.q: Find the next letter: **B, D, G, K, P, ?**
questions.solution: Gaps: B to D = +2, D to G = +3, G to K = +4, K to P = +5. Next gap +6: P (16) + 6 = 22, the 22nd letter is **V**.
questions.shortcut: Increasing gaps +2, +3, +4, +5, +6.

questions.q: Find the next group: **ACE, BDF, CEG, DFH, ?**
questions.solution: Every letter moves +1 from group to group: 1st letters A, B, C, D give **E**; 2nd letters C, D, E, F give **G**; 3rd letters E, F, G, H give **I**. Next group **EGI**.
questions.shortcut: Track each position separately: all +1.

questions.q: In a code, **TEACHER** is written as **VGCEJGT**. How will **COLLEGE** be written in that code?
questions.solution: Every letter of TEACHER moves +2 to give VGCEJGT (T to V, E to G, A to C, and so on). Shifting COLLEGE by +2: C to E, O to Q, L to N, L to N, E to G, G to I, E to G — **EQNNGIG**.
questions.shortcut: +2 shift applied to every letter.

questions.q: If **CAT** is coded as **24**, how will **DOG** be coded?
questions.solution: Code = sum of letter positions: C(3) + A(1) + T(20) = 24. So DOG = 4 + 15 + 7 = **26**.
questions.shortcut: Add the alphabet values.

questions.q:
If **×** means **+**, **+** means **÷**, **−** means **×** and **÷** means **−**, find the value of

**8 × 4 + 2 − 6 ÷ 3**
questions.solution: After the substitution the expression becomes 8 + 4 ÷ 2 × 6 − 3. BODMAS: ÷ and × first, left to right — 4 ÷ 2 = 2, then 2 × 6 = 12. Then 8 + 12 − 3 = **17**. (Solving without substituting gives 32 — a trap option.)
questions.shortcut: Rewrite with the new signs, then apply BODMAS.

questions.solution: Row rule: (first × second) + 5. Check: 4 × 7 + 5 = 33 and 5 × 3 + 5 = 20. So 6 × 2 + 5 = **17**.
questions.shortcut: first × second + 5.

questions.q: **Ravi** is the father of **Sita**. Sita is married to **Vikram**, and they have two children, **Kunal** and **Meena**. How is Meena related to Ravi?
questions.solution: Sita is Ravi's daughter, and Meena is Sita's daughter — so Meena is Ravi's **granddaughter**.
questions.shortcut: Two generations below, through the daughter.

questions.q: **A** is the brother of **B**, and B is the mother of **C**. How is A related to C?
questions.solution: A is the brother of C's mother, so A is C's maternal **uncle**.
questions.shortcut: Mother's brother = uncle.

questions.q: **Ravi** walks 5 km towards north, then turns right and walks 8 km. He turns right again and walks 5 km, then turns left and walks 4 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: North 5, then right (east) 8, right (south) 5, left (east) 4. The 5 km north and 5 km south cancel; east total = 8 + 4 = **12 km East**.
questions.shortcut: Opposite legs cancel; add same-direction legs.

questions.q: Among five trees, **A** is taller than **B** but shorter than **C**. **D** is taller than **C**, and **E** is shorter than **B**. Which tree is the second tallest?
questions.solution: Chain the clues: D > C > A > B > E. The second tallest is **C**.
questions.shortcut: Build one chain: D > C > A > B > E.

questions.q: Five friends **P, Q, R, S and T** sit in a row facing north. **R** sits exactly in the middle, **P** sits at one of the extreme ends, **Q** is an immediate neighbour of **R**, and **T** sits third to the right of **P**. Who sits **second from the left end**?
questions.solution: T is third to the right of P, so P must be at the **left** end (seat 1), putting T at seat 4. R is in the middle (seat 3). Q touches R, so Q takes seat 2 (seat 4 is taken), leaving S at seat 5. Left to right: P, Q, R, T, S. Second from the left = **Q**.
questions.shortcut: Directional clue 'third to the right' pins P's end first.

questions.q:
**Statements:** All pens are books. All books are boxes.

**Conclusions:**
I. All pens are boxes.
II. Some boxes are pens.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: Pens sit inside books, which sit inside boxes — so all pens are inside boxes (I **follows**). Pens exist, and each of them is a box, so some boxes are pens (II **follows**). Answer: **Both**.
questions.shortcut: Nested circles: A in B in C gives A in C and some C are A.

questions.solution: Every doctor and every artist is a human being (both circles inside Humans), and one person can be both a doctor and an artist (the two inner circles **overlap**). Option A shows exactly this.
questions.shortcut: Two professions inside the larger class, overlapping each other.

questions.q:
Arrange the words as in a dictionary and find the one that comes in the **middle**:

**Bracket, Braid, Bramble, Brave, Breach**
questions.solution: Compare letter by letter after Bra: **Bra**cket (c), **Bra**id (i), **Bra**mble (m), **Bra**ve (v) — c < i < m < v — and **Bre**ach comes last (e beats a at the third letter). Order: Bracket, Braid, **Bramble**, Brave, Breach. Middle = **Bramble**.
questions.shortcut: Rank by the first differing letter.

questions.q:
**Statement:** An office notice reads — all employees must submit their tax declaration forms by 30 June; forms received after this date will attract a late fee.

**Conclusions:**
I. Employees who submit the form after 30 June will have to pay a late fee.
II. No employee submits the form before June.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: I directly restates the penalty clause — **follows**. II claims nobody submits before June; the notice says nothing about early submissions — outside information, **does not follow**. Answer: **Only I**.
questions.shortcut: Restatement follows; new absolute claims do not.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 154 118" width="154" height="118" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="5" y2="113"/><line x1="5" y1="113" x2="149" y2="113"/><line x1="149" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="53" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="101" y2="113"/></svg>
questions.solution: Two lines from the apex divide the triangle. Lines through the apex = 2 cevians + the 2 sides = 4; any two of them form a triangle: C(4, 2) = **6**.
questions.shortcut: (k+1)(k+2)/2 with k = 2 gives 6.

questions.shortcut: Only characters that differ left-right actually change.

questions.q: Two different positions of the same dice are shown. Which letter is on the face opposite to **B**? (Ignore the orientation of the letters/numbers.)

questions.solution: Both views share faces A and C. With two common faces, the remaining face of each view is opposite the other: B (view 1) and D (view 2). Opposite of B is **D**.
questions.shortcut: Two common faces: the leftovers are opposite.
